projects.title: Openlyy
projects.description: An AI-powered business page that answers customer questions, collects enquiries, and keeps conversations in one inbox.

seo.title: Openlyy — Vighnesh
seo.description: An AI business page for customer questions, enquiries, and conversations. A project by Vighnesh and Karthik.

content.heading: More time for the work you love.
paragraphs: I built Openlyy with my brother, Karthik, after seeing how hard it was for our mother and other local business owners to keep up with customer messages while running their businesses.

content.heading: Your business, in a conversation.
paragraphs: Business owners add their products, services, documents, and FAQs, then share a page where customers can ask questions. The assistant uses that business information to answer, without requiring the owner to build a website or write code.

content.heading: From questions to enquiries.
paragraphs: Customers can leave contact details in the chat. Their enquiry arrives with the conversation context in the business inbox, ready for a personal follow-up. The page can be shared in a bio, a message, or an away reply.

projects.title: Box Replay
projects.description: A Mac screensaver that brings Formula 1 race data to your idle screen. Pick a race or let it choose one for you.

seo.title: Box Replay — Vighnesh
seo.description: An F1 race-data screensaver for Apple Silicon Macs, with race selection, random replay, and screen burn-in protection.

content.heading: A little more Formula 1.
paragraphs: Box Replay turns a Mac’s idle screen into a replay of Formula 1 race data. It draws on races from previous seasons, giving the screensaver something more personal than a static backdrop.

content.heading: Choose a race. Or leave it to chance.
paragraphs: Select the race you want to see, or let the screensaver pick one at random. Built-in burn-in protection is part of the screensaver experience.

content.heading: Made for the Mac.
paragraphs: The installer is designed for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 Ventura or later. It is distributed as a one-time purchase through the project’s product page.

projects.title: Wake Me After
projects.description: Choose how long you want to sleep and set your alarms in one tap. A sleep-duration alarm app for iPhone, with backup alarms and Liquid Glass.

seo.title: Wake Me After — Vighnesh
seo.description: An iPhone sleep timer that calculates your wake-up time and schedules alarms from your chosen sleep duration.

content.heading: Think in hours of sleep.
paragraphs: Wake Me After starts with how long you want to rest. Choose a duration for a quick nap or a full night’s sleep, and the app works out the wake-up time for you.

content.heading: One tap before bed.
paragraphs: Setting an alarm also supports additional buffer or backup alarms, with up to ten available. The flow keeps the focus on choosing a duration and scheduling the alarms without doing the time calculation yourself.

content.heading: Built for iOS 26.
paragraphs: The app launched on the App Store in September 2025 with an interface that uses Liquid Glass. It is designed for iPhone and requires iOS 26 or later.

projects.title: Swiggy Wrapped
projects.description: Your Swiggy order history, turned into a personalised Wrapped video. Preview it, save the video, and download snapshots, all in your browser.

seo.title: Swiggy Wrapped — Vighnesh
seo.description: A Chrome extension that turns Swiggy order history into a personalised video and downloadable snapshots, processed in the browser.

content.heading: A different kind of Wrapped.
paragraphs: Swiggy Wrapped takes the familiar annual recap idea and applies it to food orders. The extension turns a person’s Swiggy order history into a personalised video.

content.heading: Watch it. Keep it.
paragraphs: Preview the result with ten-second forward and backward seeking, then download the finished video or individual snapshots.

content.heading: Everything stays in the browser.
paragraphs: The project runs without a backend server, keeping the order data inside the browser during processing. It is an independent extension and is not affiliated with Swiggy.

projects.title: Clones
projects.description: A collection of interface recreations built with HTML and vanilla CSS, exploring layouts from music players and dashboards to messaging apps.

seo.title: Clones — Vighnesh
seo.description: Interface recreations and frontend exercises built with pure HTML and CSS, with design references, source code, and live demos.

content.heading: Learning by rebuilding.
paragraphs: Clones began as a way to understand CSS more deeply by recreating interfaces from Dribbble. I kept the exercises in vanilla CSS, without a framework, to work through the layout and styling decisions myself.

content.heading: Many interfaces. One foundation.
paragraphs: The collection includes music players, banking and analytics dashboards, email clients, messaging interfaces, and social app concepts. Each exercise explores a different combination of spacing, hierarchy, and layout.

content.heading: The references and the results.
paragraphs: The repository brings the source code together with the original design references and live demos, arranged by creation date. It also credits Jikku Jose for mentoring me through the exercises.

projects.title: Count My Shorts
projects.description: A small counter for YouTube Shorts, with usage reminders and a spacebar challenge that adds a pause to endless scrolling.

seo.title: Count My Shorts — Vighnesh
seo.description: A Chrome extension that counts YouTube Shorts, reminds you to take a break, and adds a configurable spacebar challenge.

content.heading: Make the scrolling visible.
paragraphs: Count My Shorts started as a way to interrupt my own YouTube Shorts doomscrolling. A small capsule keeps the number of shorts watched in view, making it harder to lose track of the session.

content.heading: A reminder with a little friction.
paragraphs: Usage reminders appear at an interval you choose. To continue, the extension can ask you to press the spacebar as many times as the number of shorts you have watched: 100 shorts, 100 presses.

content.heading: Set it to suit you.
paragraphs: The behaviour is configurable in the settings. The idea is to add a moment of awareness before the next scroll, rather than making every session feel the same.
